name: Slack
headline: Moderate: no review to ship, but unlisted apps get 1 channel-history request per minute.

firstTest.text: About 10 minutes, including 5 to make a free workspace: a 4-step wizard (name and workspace, scopes, events, review), then Create and Install. No review.

production.text: Same day for unlisted apps: click Activate Public Distribution and any workspace can install. Marketplace needs 10 active workspaces first, then weeks of review.

approvalWait.text: None for unlisted apps; ours was instant. Marketplace: up to 10 business days preliminary review, then up to 10 weeks functional review for new apps.

whoCanRegister.text: Anyone with a Slack account, for workspaces you're signed in to. Beyond one workspace, finish the 4-item Manage Distribution checklist; admins may still approve installs.

testMode.text: Our tokens came with no expiry and no refresh token. Rotation is opt-in (12-hour tokens). New installs of unlisted apps get 1 history request per minute.

actions.label: Send messages
actions.review: None for unlisted. The scope page gives no review note.

actions.label: Read public channel history
actions.review: No review to install. Unlisted apps get 1 request per minute on this method.

actions.label: Read private channels and DMs
actions.review: Marketplace review questions broad data-access scopes. The same rate limit applies if unlisted. Adding them showed no warning, and they were granted at once in our test install.
actions.timeToLive: same day unlisted; weeks if listing

actions.label: Post as the user
actions.review: None for unlisted. Request it as a user scope, not a bot scope.

steps.title: Create the app
steps.detail: At api.slack.com/apps, click Create an App, then Blank app (an AI agent template and a manifest option also exist). Name it and pick a signed-in workspace; you can't change it later.

steps.title: Add scopes
steps.detail: In step 2 of the wizard, search for and add bot scopes and user scopes. Each shows a plain-English line. We added 8 bot scopes and 1 user scope with no warnings.

steps.title: Add the redirect address
steps.detail: Under OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs, add your callback. It must be https, with no # anchor, and the address you send must match it.

steps.title: Build the sign-in flow
steps.detail: Send users to Slack's authorize page, asking for bot scopes and user scopes separately. Then swap the one-time code for tokens. Our sign-in returned every scope we asked for.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation
steps.detail: Opt in only after saving a redirect address. Without it our tokens never expired; with it, access lasts 12 hours, refresh tokens are single use, and you can't turn it off.

steps.title: Meet distribution requirements
steps.detail: Manage Distribution lists 4 items: features, redirect URLs, no hard-coded tokens or webhook URLs (a box you tick), and HTTPS. Three turned green once the redirect address was saved.

steps.title: Activate Public Distribution
steps.detail: One click, no review: the page switched to 'Share Your App with Any Workspace' at once. Deactivating later removes the app from other workspaces.

steps.title: Plan around the rate limit
steps.detail: Unlisted apps get 1 request per minute for channel history and thread replies, with the limit setting capped at 15. Use event pushes or webhooks instead of polling history.

steps.title: Apply for Marketplace review (optional)
steps.detail: Review is a 5-step submission needing 10 active workspaces (28 days), a privacy policy, support within 2 business days and scope justifications. Preliminary review takes up to 10 business days; functional review up to 10 weeks.

blockers.title: Your new workspace isn't in the app form
blockers.fix: The Create app form only lists workspaces this browser is signed in to. Sign in to the workspace first, then reload the form.

blockers.title: Channel history is limited to 1 request per minute
blockers.fix: It hits new unlisted commercial apps and installs after 29 May 2025. Marketplace approval removes it, and existing installs and internal customer-built apps are exempt.

blockers.title: You can't submit to Marketplace yet
blockers.fix: Slack wants at least 10 active workspaces (used in the last 28 days) before you submit. Run as an unlisted app first.

blockers.title: Workspace admins must approve your install
blockers.fix: Some workspaces require admin approval, and admins judge your scopes. Keep scopes minimal and explain each one.

blockers.title: Slack rejects your http redirect address
blockers.fix: Redirect addresses must be https, and no localhost exception is documented. Use an https tunnel in development.

blockers.title: Token rotation can't be undone
blockers.fix: Once rotation is on, you can't turn it off. Build in refresh, and save the new refresh token every time.

blockers.title: Marketplace rejects broad scopes
blockers.fix: Slack doesn't accept legacy or restricted scopes, or scopes that give broad workspace data access. Justify each scope in writing.

Provide a privacy policy and a support channel
Supply a test account and optional demo video for review
Your customers' workspace admins approve installs where required

drafts.title: App description
drafts.body: [Product] connects your AI assistant to Slack. It posts messages you ask for and reads the channels you add it to. It never reads channels it is not invited to.

drafts.title: Scope justification for review
drafts.body: chat:write: send messages the user asks the assistant to send. channels:history: read messages in channels where the app is installed so it can answer questions about them. We do not store message text beyond [N days].

drafts.title: Message for a workspace admin
drafts.body: We'd like to install [Product] in our Slack. It requests: [list scopes in plain words]. It only reads channels it is invited to. Install link: [Add to Slack URL].

unconfirmed: Whether the 1 request per minute limit has changed since the 29 May 2025 post. The page shows no later note.
Which scopes besides history ones are 'restricted' in review. The chat:write page states no restriction.
